Hi Mina / Marissa,

Two asks we want to evaluate before we finalize:

We also want to understand whether a small escrow/credit holdback or clawback can reduce our near-term risk (we'd prefer a cost offset if ramp doesn't hit).

Emily — Appreciate the detail and the forecast. Short answer: yes, we can do an interim slab + true-up and we can present both marginal and blended invoicing options. Below is a pragmatic starter proposal for HealthTech that balances your ramp risk with predictable unit economics:

Proposal (90-day interim slab) — quarter 1:
- Interim band: 0–1.2B tokens @ $0.00095/token (intro slab)
- Next band: 1.2B–3.5B tokens @ $0.00072/token (marginal rate)
- True-up: at the end of month 3 we reconcile actual tokens against committed annualized cadence; any shortfall triggers credit toward months 4–6 (no cash clawback)
- Escrow option: 10% of estimated Q1 spend held as refundable credit; released on successful ramp or applied to true-up shortfall

Marginal vs blended explanation (short):
- Marginal: tokens are billed at the rate of the band they fall into for that billing period; crossing a breakpoint only affects the tokens above breakpoint.
- Blended: a single effective per-token rate is computed for the entire usage in the period based on weighted average across bands; results in smoother invoices but can raise unit $ for the lowest usage months.

Attached is redwood_proposal_v3.pdf with worked examples using your forecast (conservative/upside). Two follow-ups:
1) Which billing model does HealthTech prefer (marginal or blended) for quarter 1?
2) If escrow is acceptable, would procurement like escrow to be applied as refundable credit or as a bank guarantee?

I'll set up a short math walkthrough with Marissa and Rishi — they'll show exact monthly examples (sample months included in the PDF).

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Revenue — Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Pricing conversation recap / ask on interim slab — internal math check

Internal notes / quick math for the call: please keep internal.

Context: HealthTech wants low near-term risk while committing annually. They prefer no cash clawback, finance will accept credit/escrow. We need to propose a clean operational true-up and a short-term bridge that doesn't create a resource scheduling headache for Dedicated pools.

Two models to show (sample month usage = 1.4B tokens):
- Marginal billing 
  - Band prices: 0–1.2B @ 0.00095; 1.2B–3.5B @ 0.00072
  - Cost = (1.2B * 0.00095) + (0.2B * 0.00072) = $1,140,000 + $144,000 = $1,284,000
- Blended billing 
  - Effective rate = ((1.2B*0.00095) + (0.2B*0.00072)) / 1.4B = $0.000917
  - Cost = 1.4B * 0.000917 = $1,283,800 (very similar this month)

Observations:
- For stepped ramps (month-to-month growth) the marginal math can create noticeable month-to-month swings when breakpoints crossed; blended compresses volatility but can slightly increase total spend in months wholly within low band.
- Escrow vs credit: escrow gives procurement comfort; refundable credit preserves cash for HealthTech and is simpler operationally for Redwood (no bank/legal overhead).

Operational asks:
- Dev: can we enforce true-up at account-level so tokens billed against the committed band are automatically reconciled? (Dev, please confirm scope for month-end reconciliation hook + invoice line item flag.)
- Rishi: suggest we include a 90-day pilot clause with a one-time right to renegotiate band thresholds if usage deviates >40% vs forecast.

Let's present both marginal and blended invoices on the math walkthrough and recommend refundable-credit escrow as default.

Mina

Emily / Nicole / Procurement — thanks for the quick turn. Following our math walkthrough and legal chat, Redwood confirms the following commercial and operational terms for signature: 

Commercial summary (agreed):
- 12-month commitment with a 90-day interim slab pilot (Q1).
- Billing model: blended-rate for months with total account usage <= 1.5B tokens; marginal billing applies for months > 1.5B.
- Breakpoints and rates (pilot): 0–1.2B @ $0.00095, 1.2B–3.5B @ $0.00072.
- True-up: month-90 reconciliation; refunds issued as refundable credits applied against months 4–6. No cash clawback during the pilot.
- Escrow: refundable credit (10% of estimated Q1 spend) — applied automatically as account credit; procurement to confirm PO cadence.
- Pilot renegotiation right: either party may request adjustments to band thresholds if realized usage deviates >40% from forecast; changes require 14 days' written notice.

Operational next steps: 
1) Marissa to send final one-page operational addendum and SOW (attached SOW_draft.docx) for internal signoff by HealthTech procurement and Redwood finance.
2) Dev to confirm the month-end reconciliation hook and invoice line-item flag (Dev, target ETA: 2027-11-06).
3) Legal (Nicole) to review refundable-credit language; Redwood will provide boilerplate.
4) Execute via DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/r/DEAL-4891 (proposal v3 sits behind link).

We can join a 30-minute signature call next week to run through the SOW and PO timing. Proposed times: Tue 2027-11-09 10:00 or Wed 2027-11-10 15:00 (PT).

Thanks — excited to get HealthTech onto Redwood and make the ramp predictable.
